ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, three identical light springs are connected at point O. The other end of spring 1 is fixed to the ceiling, and the angle with the vertical direction is $30^{\circ}$. Spring 2 is horizontal and its right end is fixed to a vertical wall. The other end of spring 3 suspends an object of mass $m$ and is in a stationary state. If at this time the deformations of springs 1, 2, and 3 are respectively $x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}$, find $x_{1}:x_{2}:x_{3}$.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, point O connects three springs; spring No. 1 is connected from point O obliquely upward to the left to the ceiling, the vertical direction is marked with a dashed line in the figure, and it is indicated that the angle between spring No. 1 and the vertical direction is 30°; spring No. 2 is connected from point O horizontally to the right to a vertical wall; spring No. 3 is connected from point O vertically downward to the suspended object. Then reason: Let the magnitudes of the pulling forces exerted by the three springs on point O be respectively T1, T2, T3. Point O is stationary, and the forces are balanced. In the horizontal direction, the horizontal component of the pulling force of spring No. 1 is to the left, with magnitude T1 sin30°, and the pulling force of spring No. 2 is to the right, with magnitude T2, so T2 = T1 sin30°. In the vertical direction, the vertical component of the pulling force of spring No. 1 is upward, with magnitude T1 cos30°, and the pulling force of spring No. 3 is downward, with magnitude T3, so T3 = T1 cos30°. The three springs are identical, the stiffness coefficients are the same, and the magnitude of the spring pulling force Ti = k xi, therefore x2 = x1 sin30° = x1/2, x3 = x1 cos30° = √3 x1/2. Thus x1:x2:x3 = 1:1/2:√3/2 = 2:1:√3.
